applies_why: The judge decides the D5/C5 collision by whether CR2 G answers the almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows and leaves the sign's sense open, so the rule governing chain-against-chain weighing applies.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase 'chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse' could mean either that the judge must assess the integrated footing of the pressing chain and the link chain, or that a short row-by-row/open-sense statement can satisfy the rule; I weighed those readings.
why: Because the judge rests the underdetermination on answered individual rows and an open sign-sense rather than on a chain-against-chain footing comparison, it fails K-C.
